messages.subject: Two questions about MLR
parts:
Hi,

I wonder if you guys can answer me two questions.

1. I know of a major test for model comparison for MLR models: Satorra-Bentler Scaled Chi-Square Difference Test. The one being used by lavaan is another test - Yuan-Bentler Chi-Square Difference test, am I correct? In my field, people only talk about Satorra-Bentler Scaled Chi-Square Difference Test. Is it possible to ask lavaan to conduct Satorra-Bentler Chi-Sqaure Difference Test instead of the Yuan-Bentler one?

2. I just wonder if there is an easy way to conduct Satorra-Bentler Strictly Positive Scaled Chi-Square Difference Test? Editors and Reviewers keep asking for it, even though it is quite troublesome to conduct it by hand in Mplus.

Thank you very much for answering my questions.

Chester

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Two questions about MLR
parts:
On 12/17/2013 01:09 PM, Chester Kam wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I wonder if you guys can answer me two questions.
>
> 1. I know of a major test for model comparison for MLR models:
> Satorra-Bentler Scaled Chi-Square Difference Test. The one being used by
> lavaan is another test - Yuan-Bentler Chi-Square Difference test, am I
> correct?

No.

If you have used MLR, it is always the Yuan-Bentler version. If you want
Satorra-Bentler, simply use estimator="MLM" for both models. But
remember that MLM only works for complete data.

Think of Yuan-Bentler as a modern version of Satorra-Bentler. There is
nothing wrong with it.

> 2. I just wonder if there is an easy way to conduct Satorra-Bentler
> Strictly Positive Scaled Chi-Square Difference Test? Editors and
> Reviewers keep asking for it, even though it is quite troublesome to
> conduct it by hand in Mplus.

Well, here is the good news: lavaan already gives you this 'strictly'
positive scaled difference test, for free. Because lavaan uses the
original Satorra (2000) formulas. You get it automatically when you are
using the anova() function on two (or more) models with scaled test
statistics.

The trouble with 'negative' values only occurs if you are using the
popular Satorra & Bentler (2001) simplification, which you can get from
lavaan if you pass the (hidden) option 'SB.classic=TRUE' to the anova
function.

In lavaan 0.5-16, there is new function lavTestLRT() (called by anova())
which contains proper documentation and references.

Yves.
